query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount of Sn into single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys can increase the coercive field by inducing a phase transformation from fcc to bcc.
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Sn
generation.conditions: Room temperature, applied magnetic field of 1 T
generation.structural_mediator: Phase transformation from fcc to bcc
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, as the addition of Sn can induce a phase transformation from fcc to bcc, which can increase the coercive field.
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys with a coercive field of no greater than 100 Oe
generation.boundary: Compositional boundary: 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10, where x is the amount of Sn added
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Sn required to induce the phase transformation and increase the coercive field is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys with varying amounts of Sn (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) and measure the coercive field using VSM measurements at an applied magnetic field of 1 T.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field does not increase with the addition of Sn, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How does the addition of Sn (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) affect the phase constitution, microstructure, and magnetic properties (specifically saturation magnetization, remanence, and Curie temperature) of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 high-entropy alloys?. System: FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10). Processing: Vacuum arc-melting of 99.99% purity constituent elements using a water-cooled Cu crucible, followed by suction casting into a 100 × 10× 2 mm water-cooled Cu mold after remelting four times.. Test conditions: XRD scan speed of 1°/min; VSM measurements at an applied magnetic field of 1 T; HCTS hysteresis curves using a 27 × 9 × 1.7 mm rectangular sample at a magnetic field of 25 kA/m; DSC thermal stability analysis at a heating rate of 10 K/min.. Findings: The ratio of I(110)BCC/I(111)FCC increases from 0.38 (x=0) to 10.53 (x=0.10), indicating a rapid increase in BCC phase content.; Saturation magnetization (Ms) increases from 78.6 Am2/kg to 88.8 Am2/kg as x increases f
